articles.title: Tom Brady’s property moves from Boston to Miami: A look at the real estate decisions behind the seven-time champion’s next chapter
articles.summary: Tom Brady no longer owns property in Massachusetts.
articles.body: Tom Brady no longer owns property in Massachusetts. The Brookline mansion he built with Gisele Bündchen sold on Christmas Eve 2020, and his biggest real estate project now sits on Indian Creek Island in Miami. The lot cost $17 million in 2020. In January 2025, Bloomberg reported that the newly finished house had drawn bids above $150 million, though no sale has been confirmed. Between those two addresses sits a story about timing, patience and how a quarterback learned to treat housing as a business.How Tom Brady's property base shifted from Boston to MiamiThe move started well before the quarterback left New England. Brady and Bündchen listed 112 Woodland Road in August 2019 at $39.5 million, then cut the price to $33.9 million two months later. Brady joined the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in March 2020, and the house was still there. It came off the market as COVID-19 hurt luxury sales, then returned quietly as an off-market listing.The deal closed on December 24, 2020. The deed showed a price of $1 and named a trustee as the buyer, who may not have been the final owner. Boston real estate circles believed the property was offered at $32.5 million. Nobody involved has confirmed a number.The Miami purchase landed in the same stretch. Forbes reported that the couple paid $17 million late in 2020 for a tear-down property on Indian Creek Island. Their Manhattan apartment also sold for nearly $37 million around then. Within months, three big holdings became one big plan.A Tampa contract explains why Brady wanted to be in Florida. It does not explain why he picked Miami, which sits across the state. That choice reads like a decision about life after football, not just the next season.Why the Brookline mansion took so long to sellThe house was not a small ask. It was built in 2015 on about five acres beside The Country Club, and it covers 12,112 square feet. Buyers at that price are rare, and the pool shrinks further when a pandemic keeps people at home.Neighbors faced the same wall. Paul Fireman's mansion down the street sold for $23 million in 2020, after it was listed at $90 million in 2016. Against that backdrop, Brady's sale looks less like a failure and more like a reasonable exit. If the reported $32.5 million is right, he came away about 18 percent below his first ask.The private route also made sense. Off-market sales keep prices out of public view, and that protects a seller who has already cut once. Brady lost some money on paper but avoided a public markdown fight, which is a trade many owners at this level choose.What Tom Brady built on Indian Creek IslandIndian Creek is a man-made island with about 40 residences, a country club and its own police department. It is known as the Billionaire Bunker, and Jeff Bezos has bought two homes there.Brady did not keep the original house. The two-acre lot now holds a two-story home with a security building, gym, cabana, pool and sport court, according to property documents. The address is 26 Indian Creek Island Road. Reports differ on timing. Bloomberg called the house newly finished in early 2025, while other outlets date completion to early 2026, so the build clearly ran long.The money behind it is partly visible. The Real Deal reportedly found a $35 million construction loan from Citizens Bank in July 2024. That is a normal way to fund a custom build, even for someone with Brady's income.He also spread his base. He owns a 14,000-square-foot estate in Brentwood, California, that he was renovating, and he set up office space for his family business in Bay Harbor, close to Indian Creek.Is the $150 million Miami house really for sale?Not officially. Bloomberg reported that the property was being shown to a small group of buyers, with no public listing. The $150 million figure came from bids, not a closed deal. Later coverage in 2026 still describes it as a reported price, and I found no confirmed sale or listing.If a deal did close near that number, it would top the $107 million Ken Griffin paid for a Coconut Grove estate in 2022 and set a Miami record. The gap with Brady's costs is also worth noting. A $17 million lot plus a multi-year build does not equal profit. Construction, financing and carrying costs eat into any headline price.What stands out is the pattern. Brady sold high-profile homes quietly, held land through a long build, and tested the market without a listing. Whether he sells or stays, the Miami house is now his main real estate story.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "Caught me b**ging an NFL head coach": Mike Vrabel scandal follows Dianna Russini as NFL analyst questions her return to the spotlight
articles.summary: Dianna Russini may be preparing to reclaim her place in NFL media, but her reported comeback is already facing criticism.
articles.body: Dianna Russini may be preparing to reclaim her place in NFL media, but her reported comeback is already facing criticism. Months after her departure from The Athletic following controversy surrounding New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, the former NFL insider appears ready to return to the spotlight. However, not everyone believes the move makes sense. WFAN radio host Gregg Giannotti has openly questioned why Russini would want to return to the same industry, particularly after the controversy damaged her professional standing and brought intense public scrutiny.Gregg Giannotti questions Dianna Russini’s NFL return after Mike Vrabel controversyRussini's reported plans to return to NFL coverage became a talking point after Pro Football Talk revealed on Wednesday that she had started contacting people across the league about her next professional move. According to the report, she told industry contacts that she would be returning to work "next week."The news caught Giannotti's attention during Thursday's episode of Boomer & Gio. Rather than welcoming the possibility of her comeback, the radio personality questioned why Russini would choose to remain in football journalism when other career opportunities were available."Why, in this business? Why not something else? Anything," Giannotti said. "Go work at a hotel. Be the person who fills out the waivers when you go on the banana boat in the Bahamas. Anywhere, just get out of here."He also suggested that familiarity with an industry can make it difficult for someone to consider a fresh start, even when their professional circumstances change.“I think she was trying to think about, ‘How do I get back into the NFL and do all these things that I did in the NFL?’ Just like many people, I don’t think it [change] crosses their minds. This is what I know, and this is what I do, as opposed to taking a risk and trying something different,” added.Giannotti then made his position even clearer with a blunt personal comparison.“I’ll tell you right now. If someone caught me banging an NFL head coach, I’d be out of here,” he said.Dianna Russini’s Mike Vrabel scandal continues to follow her careerRussini resigned from The Athletic on April 14, shortly after Page Six published photographs showing her with Vrabel at a hotel in Sedona, Arizona. Some images showed the two hugging and holding hands, triggering widespread speculation about their relationship.Both figures denied any wrongdoing. Vrabel described the interaction as innocent, while Russini maintained that the photographs did not represent the larger group of six people who had spent time together that day.The controversy did not end with her resignation. A September review by The Athletic examined 903 stories, 77 videos and 204 podcast episodes. It found no clear evidence of bias towards Vrabel's teams but concluded that Russini's undisclosed relationship violated the publication's standards, regardless of whether it was romantic.Meanwhile, her next destination remains uncertain. Front Office Sports reported that Russini was almost certainly the mystery host of a new weekly NFL programme planned by BetUS. The company was expected to reveal its host on Monday.For now, Russini's reported comeback has raised another question: Can she rebuild her career in the same NFL media landscape where the controversy unfolded?Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ $325 million KC Current face another defining moment after stunning NWSL playoff twist
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have another reason to celebrate as the Kansas City Current continue their push for NWSL glory.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have another reason to celebrate as the Kansas City Current continue their push for NWSL glory. The club, which the couple co-owns, delivered a crucial playoff performance at CPKC Stadium, defeating Angel City FC 1-0 after extra time on Saturday. The victory carries special significance for Kansas City after last year's disappointing quarterfinal exit on home soil. This time, the Current found a way through, keeping their championship hopes alive and giving their supporters a memorable moment in front of their home crowd.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes celebrate KC Current's NWSL playoff breakthroughThe Kansas City Current had plenty riding on this quarterfinal clash. Playing at home brought both an advantage and added pressure, especially after their previous postseason campaign ended earlier than expected.Angel City FC arrived in strong form, having gone unbeaten across its previous 10 matches, with eight victories and two draws. The visitors also looked dangerous during the opening stages, creating some of the better scoring opportunities and forcing Kansas City to work hard defensively.However, the Current gradually took control. They struggled to find the finishing touch during the first half, but their attacking intent became increasingly clear as the match progressed.Kansas City finished regulation time with 16 shots compared to Angel City's seven. The home side also produced 10 attempts in the second half alone, putting sustained pressure on the visitors' defence.Despite creating several promising opportunities, the Current could not find a breakthrough during the initial 90 minutes. The match went into extra time, where Kansas City continued to push forward and threatened through multiple corner kicks.KC Current keep championship dreams alive with dramatic extra-time victoryThe decisive moment finally arrived in extra time when Kansas City earned a penalty kick. After spending much of the contest searching for a way past Angel City's stubborn defence, the opportunity gave the home side its chance to settle the contest.The resulting 1-0 victory sent the Current into the NWSL semifinals, turning a tense afternoon into a celebration for the players and supporters.For Patrick and Brittany Mahomes, the result also marks an important moment for their investment in women's professional soccer. The couple joined the ownership group of the Kansas City Current in 2023, alongside other prominent investors, helping strengthen the club's profile.Patrick has built his reputation through his success with the Kansas City Chiefs, but his involvement in the Current reflects a wider interest in the city's sporting future. Brittany has also played an active role in the club's ownership journey.Now, the Current have taken another important step towards the NWSL title. Their quarterfinal victory not only erases last season's disappointment but also puts them closer to delivering another major sporting achievement for Kansas City.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patriots Trade Rumor: Unexpected Name Could Be on Move at Deadline
articles.summary: The NFL Trade Deadline is rapidly approaching on Tuesday, November 10th. With that, rumors are swirling around how the New England Patriots could be getting...
articles.body:
The NFL Trade Deadline is rapidly approaching on Tuesday, November 10th. With that, rumors are swirling around how the New England Patriots could be getting ready to prepare for their next playoff run.

Most fans think first and foremost about adding players at the deadline. However, there have also been rumors that the Patriots could potentially move on from several players.

The conversation about moving on from Patriots players has largely focused on the defensive side of the ball. Still, the opportunity to move players goes beyond that. Dan Graziano of ESPN even recently shared that the focus could be on quarterback Tommy DeVito.

Could the New England Patriots Move Tommy DeVito?

Luckily, the Patriots haven't had much reason to think about the backup quarterback position this season. Drake Maye has bounced back from his slow start and stayed healthy. So, Tommy DeVito has largely remained on the bench while Behren Morton acts as the team's third-string option.

Other teams around the NFL haven't been so lucky. Injuries abound and several playoff contenders are without a healthy starting quarterback. So, it makes sense to Graziano that the Patriots could get calls about him, and that they'd move him for the right price.

"Quarterback Tommy DeVito," Graziano wrote . "I don't think the Patriots are trading players. However, DeVito is a backup quarterback with NFL starting experience, so it's not wild to think New England could get a call."

DeVito is in his second season with the Patriots. He had previously played for the New York Giants , where he developed a bit of a cult following and did have experience as a starter. In New England, he's played in one game. That was in relief during the blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season.

The rumors around the New England Patriots go well beyond DeVito. That includes the idea that they could move a player like Carlton Davis or Christian Barmore from the defense. Then, there's the idea that they could bring in a wide receiver or a running back to help address injury concerns.

Seth Walder of ESPN isn't thinking skill positions. Instead, he thinks if the Patriots add, it will be to the offensive line.

" Saints G Cesar Ruiz ," Walder wrote. "Both of the Patriots' Week 1 starters at guard — Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Mike Onwenu (ankle) — are on injured reserve. In Ruiz, New England would be adding a starting-caliber guard who is having a particularly good season, with a 78th percentile pass block win rate. He's a better pass protector than run blocker, but the former is more important in New England where protecting Drake Maye is the most important job of the offensive line."

There may be something to that from Walder. The Athletic recently reported that the Patriots shouldn't expect a move at wide receiver or running back. That, of course, leaves room to add on defense or along the offensive line.

Still, there are a couple of days for things to change. The NFL Trade Deadline isn't until 4:00 p.m. EST on Tuesday, November 1oth.

articles.title: Sam Darnold Injured, Latest Rumors as QB 'in Danger of Missing' More Games for Seahawks
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will be sidelined with a quad injury for Sunday's matchup against the visiting Arizona Cardinals and reportedly may also be out for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will be sidelined with a quad injury for Sunday's matchup against the visiting Arizona Cardinals and reportedly may also be out for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders.

ESPN's Adam Schefter , citing league sources, reported on Sunday that Darnold "is in danger of missing Seattle's Week 10 game against the Raiders." Schefter added that "Darnold could attempt to try to return for next Sunday's game in Las Vegas, but the Seahawks also know that they have their bye the following week. By missing the next two games, Darnold could get the chance to rest the next three weeks before the Seahawks play a big divisional Week 12 game in San Francisco against the 49ers."

Darnold is considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald.

Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of Monday's loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald.

Macdonald clarified it is the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action.

Drew Lock is dealing with an elbow injury but if available is slated to start with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals, Macdonald said.

The Seahawks don't currently have any other quarterbacks on the roster. Macdonald didn't rule out the possibility of adding another signal caller ahead of Sunday's game.

Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions.

Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold.

The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos.

Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs.

Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can."

As of Wednesday, Macdonald said Lock was "able to throw" but that his capacity would be determined during practice this week.

Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks.

The Seahawks (4-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (6-1).

A win this week over the Cardinals (3-5) would increase the defending champions' playoff odds to 54 percent, while a loss would drop the team to 29 percent, according to NFL Next Gen Stats .

How much participation Lock sees in practice this week could provide an early indication as to whether Milroe will be making his first NFL start in a crucial divisional matchup this weekend.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders' Rumored QB2 Revealed Between Deshaun Watson, Dillon Gabriel for Browns vs. Saints
articles.summary: Dillon Gabriel will back up Shedeur Sanders at quarterback for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.
articles.body:
Dillon Gabriel will back up Shedeur Sanders at quarterback for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

The Browns listed Deshaun Watson as questionable in their injury report as he recovered from a concussion. He missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday and was limited for Friday's workout.

Watson has reportedly cleared the NFL's concussion protocol, but Cleveland isn't taking any risks with the three-time Pro Bowler.

The Browns' overall performance made it tough for coach Todd Monken to change quarterbacks despite Watson being inconsistent. The veteran signal-caller has thrown for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions, and he ranks 28th among qualified passers in QBR (40.9), per ESPN.com .

The 31-year-old briefly exited Cleveland's 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. The team said he was evaluated for a concussion on the sideline and cleared. He was assessed following the contest and then again Monday. It wasn't until Tuesday he began to experience concussion-like symptoms.

Monken confirmed Friday that Sanders will get the nod against New Orleans. After that, moving Gabriel up one spot in the depth chart felt like the obvious solution to the backup situation.

The southpaw hasn't seen the field since last December. As a rookie, he had 937 yards, seven touchdowns and two picks in 10 appearances.

If everything goes according to plan for the Browns, Gabriel's wait for meaningful snaps will extend for at least another week.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson's Message to Ravens Revealed in NFL Rumors amid Injury, Return Buzz and Losing Streak
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is aiming to return during the 2026 NFL season, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is aiming to return during the 2026 NFL season, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Rapoport reported that Jackson spoke to the team and delivered an "energizing" and "exciting" message. The overall theme was to "just stay alive" until he's healthy enough to be back on the field.

The Ravens are last in the AFC North at 4-5 following Thursday's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The combined absences of Jackson and Tyler Huntley were glaring as third-stringer Joe Fagnano threw for 60 yards and two interceptions on 18 attempts.

Jackson has unfortunately had another injury-riddled year.

After playing the first three games of the year, he missed three games because of a high ankle sprain, returning to action on Nov. 1 against the Buffalo Bills. His return was brief, however, as he suffered a thumb injury on the Ravens' first offensive drive.

The injury required surgery, and the two-time MVP was placed on the injured reserve immediately after the game.

Huntley came in for Jackson after his injury, but he was forced to exit soon after because of a turf toe injury.

A day after the Jaguars loss, Baltimore acquired Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. Brissett is a significant upgrade from Fagnano and may be enough for the team to keep its head above water in the weeks ahead.

It's clear Jackson isn't throwing away the rest of the season, and that attitude is bound to spread to the rest of the locker room.

articles.title: New Derrick Henry Trade Rumors on Teams Still Interested in RB Despite Ravens' Stance on Deadline
articles.summary: Teams around the NFL remain hopeful the Baltimore Ravens will consider trading star running back Derrick Henry, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
Teams around the NFL remain hopeful the Baltimore Ravens will consider trading star running back Derrick Henry, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Schefter reported Sunday the Ravens "keep telling teams he's not available" with Tuesday's trade deadline quickly approaching.

Henry hasn't been a source of regular trade speculation, at least to the extent the Indianapolis Colts' Jonathan Taylor has . But teams might as well ask the question when injuries to quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley have cast a shadow on the Ravens' playoff hopes.

Baltimore isn't throwing in the towel, though. The team worked out a deal to acquire Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals, which will stabilize the quarterback room.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport also reported Sunday that Jackson, who needs surgery for a thumb injury, told his teammates he's aiming to return this season.

Jonathan Jones of The Athletic suggested a Henry trade could have wider implications with Jackson under contract for one more season: "Would [Jackson] leave the Ravens? One of the quickest ways to make that hypothetical a reality would be to trade Derrick Henry."

That's unlikely to become an issue. Making a short-term, win-now trade for Brissett and immediately dealing a massive blow to your backfield by offloading Henry makes little sense.

Because of that, it's safe to assume the five-time Pro Bowler will remain in Baltimore through the deadline.

articles.title: Why Jim Harbaugh, Chargers Won't Trade Justin Herbert, McConkey, Mack Revealed in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: Despite owning an 0-7 record, the Los Angeles Chargers don't like the optics of being a seller ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
Despite owning an 0-7 record, the Los Angeles Chargers don't like the optics of being a seller ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Schefter reported the Chargers and coach Jim Harbaugh "don't like the message of giving up on the season."

Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Saturday L.A. is indicating to any interested suitors its biggest trade assets, including Khalil Mack, Justin Herbert and Ladd McConkey, are unavailable.

Harbaugh has never had a losing record as an NFL coach, and his competitive drive sets him apart from some of his peers.

Alas, this is one situation where discretion is the better part of valor.

No NFL team has reached the playoffs after dropping its first seven games, and the Chargers have supplied little in the way of evidence leading you to believe a turnaround is imminent. Herbert's performance in particular is concerning.

Holding onto Herbert and McConkey is at least justifiable.

Harbaugh has gone over the top in the past to praise his starting quarterback, and the two-time Pro Bowler is under contract through 2029. You can rationalize building around Herbert next year and beyond if you still believe in him.

Similarly, McConkey's rookie deal runs for one more season, and he'll turn 25 in a few days. He can be a long-term piece in the passing game regardless of how disastrous 2026 has been.

Mack is the trade asset that's almost impossible to rationalize keeping. He's a free agent at the end of the year, and he has already contemplated retirement once.

Schefter and Rapoport reported the Chargers "prioritized keeping Mack for the leadership he provides and talent he brings." From a talent perspective, the 35-year-old is clearly past his peak, and the intangible benefits of his leadership are mitigated when things are so bad for the team.

The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported that Los Angeles' approach to the deadline "has confounded rival teams who wish to peck at the Chargers' carcass before Tuesday." Jones added that some around the NFL "pointed to the head coach specifically" for why the organization is so steadfast.

That won't be a comforting thought for fans who think Harbaugh may have lost his touch . Being unable to adapt and accept short-term pain for long-term gain is a recipe for eventual mediocrity or worse.

articles.summary: Jeffery Simmons and Montez Sweat anchor a surging Bears defense as Chicago hosts Tampa Bay on Sunday Night Football in their third straight primetime game.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson reportedly expected to miss 6-9 weeks, is telling teammates he'll return this season
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson wants to return to help the Ravens this season.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is determined to return before the end of the 2026 NFL season. Jackson, who is expected to miss between six and nine weeks, reportedly told teammates to " just stay alive " ahead of his return, according to ESPN.

Jackson reportedly sustained a fractured and dislocated thumb during the team's Week 8 game against the Buffalo Bills. Jackson, who was making his first start since Week 4, was injured on his first passing attempt of the contest after his thumb made contact with the hand of Bills defender Greg Rousseau, who was trying to disrupt the pass.

Jackson left the game, and was replaced by Tyler Huntley, who also got injured in the contest. On Thursday, the team placed both Jackson and Huntley on injured reserve . Huntley's injury — turf toe — is said to be season-ending.

The team kept things close to the vest with Jackson, not revealing the extent of his injury Thursday. When asked whether Jackson would miss the rest of the season, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter merely said, " we'll see. "

Given the timeline, Jackson's return is far from guaranteed. If he needs closer to nine weeks to return, Jackson would be looking to come back in early January. At that point, the team could be out of the playoff hunt.

Reaching the postseason without both Jackson and Huntley could prove difficult. A loss to the Bills in Week 8 dropped the team to 4-4 on the season. With both players sidelined, the Ravens turned to third-stringer Joe Fagnano in Week 9. He struggled during a 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, dropping the Ravens to 4-5.

Before that game, however, the team signaled it planned to contend down the stretch. On Wednesday, it was reported the team acquired veteran Jacoby Brissett in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals. Brissett wasn't ready to play Thursday, but will likely move into a starting role as soon as he's up to speed.

Whether Brissett can keep the team afloat long enough for Jackson to return remains to be seen. It should help, however, that the Ravens' next four opponents are currently under .500.

It's imperative the team come out of that stretch with a strong record. Baltimore closes out the season with four straight AFC North games, all against teams with winning records.

articles.title: New Jets Trade Rumors Leak on Positions to Watch and Stance on 2026 NFL Deadline
articles.summary: The New York Jets "don't expect to be very active" prior to Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, according to ESPN's Rich Cimini.
articles.body:
The New York Jets "don't expect to be very active" prior to Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, according to ESPN's Rich Cimini .

Cimini posited New York possesses "a surplus of safeties" that could be leveraged for some draft capital or perhaps some reinforcements along the defensive line.

Broadly speaking, though, the Jets aren't "going to trade an asset that could help in the future" when their focus is on 2027 and beyond.

General manager Darren Mougey laid out the overall aim for 2026 when he rolled into the year with Geno Smith at quarterback. New York is treading water until next spring, when it will have three first-round picks and a ton of salary cap space .

The fanbase doesn't like watching a 2-6 team, but it can see the strategy being put into place.

Improvement can unfold quickly in the NFL. The Las Vegas Raiders have already surpassed their win total from 2025. The New England Patriots went from back-to-back 4-13 finishes to the Super Bowl after hiring Mike Vrabel.

Mougey doesn't need to tear the roster down to the studs because he has effectively done that already.

The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported the Jets "have no desire or intention to trade wide receiver Garrett Wilson or running back Breece Hall."

"These two players are pieces of the team's foundation in what is supposed to be a turnaround year," Jones wrote.

Wilson and Hall are both in their mid-20s, and they're signed through 2030 and 2028, respectively. They should be considered long-term focal points for the offense.

Flipping Quinnen Williams and Sauce Gardner, the latter in particular, for prime draft capital looks even savvier in retrospect. Sooner or later, a front office's priorities have to shift, and appears that has happened for Mougey.

articles.title: New Patriots Trade Rumors on A.J. Brown's Impact on 2026 NFL Deadline and Latest Plans
articles.summary: The New England Patriots reportedly won't be generating significant headlines by Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, and the previous acquisition of star receiver A.J. Brown has something to do with that strategy.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots reportedly won't be generating significant headlines by Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, and the previous acquisition of star receiver A.J. Brown has something to do with that strategy.

ESPN's Mike Reiss reported Sunday that "fireworks aren't expected with the Patriots" when it comes to major trades. Instead, they could look to make some "modest moves" like they were known for when Bill Belichick was the head coach, such as when they acquired linebacker Kyle Van Noy and a seventh-round pick for a sixth-round pick in 2016.

"There are multiple reasons, according to sources familiar with the team's thinking, and near the top of the list is the unwillingness to sacrifice significant assets from future Patriots teams," Reiss wrote. "The club already did that in the offseason by trading a 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fifth-rounder for receiver A.J. Brown in June, which was part of an overall aggressive offseason."

The Brown trade isn't the only reason there could be hesitance from the Patriots to make any high-profile acquisitions.

Reiss explained they leave for Munich on Wednesday ahead of their game in Germany against the Detroit Lions, which would limit the amount of time they could bring any acquired player in and have him ready to go for the next game.

What's more, they have just $5 million in salary cap space and will need some of it for elevating players from the practice squad and bringing others off injured reserve. They simply don't have significant space to add highly paid players at this point of the season.

New England could look at Brown as something of an acquisition for the stretch run, though, when he does return to the lineup.

He has appeared in just three games this season and will miss Sunday's contest against the Green Bay Packers because of ankle and knee injuries.

The offense has adjusted to his absence and relied on tight end Hunter Henry and running back Rhamondre Stevenson in the aerial attack. Wide receivers DeMario Douglas and Romeo Doubs have also been key factors.

Still, the Patriots brought Brown in to be their go-to receiver for quarterback Drake Maye. He surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of the previous four seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles, including when he went over 1,400 in back-to-back years in 2022 and 2023.

At his best, he is one of the league's elite receivers who opens up the entire field for the rest of his teammates because of the attention he draws.

While the Patriots reportedly won't be adding headline players at the deadline, adding that version of Brown would open up their offense for the stretch run.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Has Giants VP 'In Awe' After Concerns About 'Maturity Level' Before NFL Draft 2024
articles.summary: J.J. McCarthy looks "completely different" to New York Giants senior vice president of player personnel Chris Mara than he did when the NFC East team decided not to select him with the No. 6 overall pick of the 2024 NFL draft.
articles.body:
J.J. McCarthy looks "completely different" to New York Giants senior vice president of player personnel Chris Mara than he did when the NFC East team decided not to select him with the No. 6 overall pick of the 2024 NFL draft.

"We had him rated very high from a skill set," Mara told Steve Serby of the New York Post when discussing the quarterback the Giants traded for this season. "… We weren't quite sure about the maturity level, but we loved his skill set. He showed the ability to win, the ability to lead. Seeing him three years later, this is a completely different-looking person for me."

Mara continued and said McCarthy looks different "on the field and off the field. He's a terrific guy, he's matured, he's married now, has a kid. I'm in awe when I watch him in practice. He's got a much better arm than I thought he ever had. He moves around great. Listen, the arrow's up on him, too."

The Giants didn't draft McCarthy, but they used that No. 6 pick on a game-changer in wide receiver Malik Nabers. They also landed a potential franchise quarterback in the next draft when they selected Jaxson Dart in the first round in 2025.

However, Dart's injury this season forced the team into scramble mode, and they ended up trading for McCarthy after the Michigan product never completely found his footing on the Minnesota Vikings and found himself behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz on the depth chart.

McCarthy didn't live up to expectations in Minnesota as the No. 10 overall pick of that 2024 draft, but the Giants trade has given him a new opportunity and a change of scenery.

He threw for 243 yards in one quarter of action against the New Orleans Saints to earn a start against the Houston Texans. He then threw for 252 yards in an overtime victory over the Texans and is the surefire starter heading into Sunday's contest against the Philadelphia Eagles.

In something of an ironic twist, McCarthy's No. 1 receiver now is the player the Giants took over him in the 2024 draft. Nabers exploded for 111 receiving yards in the win over the Texans, which was his fourth straight game over the century mark.

While Dart will surely battle to get his job back when he is healthy next season, the Giants are relying on two top-10 picks of the 2024 draft to elevate their aerial attack for the immediate future.

And they are in first place in the NFC East with plenty of momentum heading into Sunday's contest.

articles.title: NFL Trade Deadline 2026 Date, End Time, Hottest Rumors, Predictions and More
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline will arrive at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10. While teams still have time to make moves, we've already seen a flood of activity on the trade market.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline will arrive at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10. While teams still have time to make moves, we've already seen a flood of activity on the trade market.

Big names like Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Marvin Harrison Jr., and Jeffery Simmons were traded well ahead of the deadline. On Friday, the Baltimore Ravens and Arizona Cardinals officially announced a trade that will send quarterback Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore.

While the trade activity may pause for Sunday's slate of games, we can expect more trades to come through the transaction wire before Tuesday's deadline. Which players and teams could dominate the upcoming news cycle? Let's dive into the latest buzz.

Titans Listening to Tony Pollard, Calvin Ridley Offers

The Simmons deal may have a massive impact on this year's playoff race, as the star defensive tackle immediately shined for the Chicago Bears last Monday. The Tennessee Titans may not be done making high-impact trades.

According to ProFootballTalk's Mike Florio , "multiple teams" are interested in Titans running back Tony Pollard, who has 665 scrimmage yards and six touchdowns this season.

Pollard is set to be a free agent in 2027. However, keeping him would make some sense for the Titans, who are still in the evaluation stage with second-year quarterback Cam Ward. That doesn't mean he's entirely off-limits, though.

Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer reported on Friday that the Titans "have listened" to offers for Pollard and wide receiver Calvin Ridley.

Of the two players, Ridley should be viewed as the more expendable. Pollard has been an offensive centerpiece, especially recently. Ridley has dramatically fallen out of the offensive game plan after being a 1,000-yard receiver two years ago.

So far this season, Ridley has just six catches for 91 yards on 13 targets.

Prediction: Titans keep Pollard, trade Ridley for a late-round pick

Colts Want a 'Christian McCaffrey-Type Package' for Jonathan Taylor

The Indianapolis Colts will face the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, and they should have star running back Jonathan Taylor in the lineup. However, Taylor has been a popular trade target ahead of the deadline and could be moved by Tuesday.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport recently reported that "several teams" are interested in Taylor and are willing to offer significant compensation to get him. However, Rapoport also noted that the Colts don't really want to move their offensive centerpiece and want a "Christian McCaffrey-type package" in return for him.

The Carolina Panthers traded McCaffrey to the San Francisco 49ers in 2022 and received 2023 second-, third-, and fourth-round picks, along with a 2024 fifth-rounder.

As Rapoport noted, the Colts haven't received that sort of offer yet, or else Taylor would already be gone. However, Rapoport also reported on Good Morning Football earlier in the week that the Colts are "open" to trading Taylor (beginning around the 1:00 mark).

Indy has already fired general manager Chris Ballard and will likely be rebuilding with a new front office and quarterback in 2027. The prediction here is that the Colts ultimately decide to move Taylor in order to jump-start that rebuild.

Prediction: Taylor is traded at the deadline

Jets Don't Plan to Trade Breece Hall, Garrett Wilson

New York Jets receiver Garrett Wilson will miss Week 9 with a concussion, but running back Breece Hall is expected to return from his quad injury. Both players have been the topic of trade speculation in recent weeks.

Wilson hasn't been as productive in the Jets' passing attack, as fellow receivers Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. have started to take off. While Hall has been out, Braelon Allen has looked like the sort of starting-caliber back who could make Hall expendable.

However, one source told ESPN's Adam Schefter last week that there is "no way" that New York will move either player at the deadline. While that was before the Jets dropped their sixth game of the season, signs continue to point to them being non-sellers at the deadline.

"I would be surprised if the Jets moved running back Breece Hall or other major players based on conversations this week," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler wrote on Wednesday. "The Jets do not appear to be in the mode to deal talent."

New York appears to be preparing for a new quarterback to be added in 2027. If the Jets intend for him to be a plug-and-play starter, tearing down their talented young offensive cast wouldn't make much sense.

Prediction: Jets hang onto both Wilson and Hall

The Titans and Colts may not be in full-on fire-sale mode after dealing notable veterans ahead of deadline week. The Philadelphia Eagles, however, may be open to moving multiple players.

The Eagles are stuck in what appears to be a lost season. Jalen Hurts is unlikely to return in 2026 as he continues to deal with blood clots. Offensive stars like Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith have not been healthy. At 2-6, Philadelphia is in the NFC East basement.

According to Breer , the Eagles have multiple veterans available:

"The Eagles' six-game losing streak obviously opens up the possibility that they'd move some contract-year vets, and Hollywood Brown, Riq Woolen, Dallas Goedert, Michael Carter II and now Tanner McKee are among those perceived by other teams to be available."

Eagles GM Howie Roseman has already traded center Cam Jurgens, and he probably won't stand pat between now and the deadline. According to Breer, though, he won't be trading defensive tackle Moro Ojomo.

Prediction: Philadelphia deals Marquise Brown and Riq Woolen before the deadline

articles.title: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers
articles.summary: The Buccaneers are coming off two straight wins, including a shutout win over Atlanta.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears hype is about to get very loud.

This NFL season seems wide open. There isn't one great team yet and there are few trustworthy contenders who have emerged. The Bears seemingly saw it the same way when they traded two first-round picks for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.

And through one game, it seems like a transformative trade. The Bears had a fantastic performance on a national stage, shutting down the Seahawks in a 34-17 win . Chicago's Super Bowl odds took a leap, as did Caleb Williams' MVP odds. In a season dying for a dominant team to emerge, maybe it's Chicago.

The Bears' offense isn't a question. It has scored 30 points in every game Williams has started and finished (it did score just three points against the Vikings and Williams played three-and-a-half quarters, but that says something about Minnesota's defense). If Simmons has as big of an impact on the defense as it appeared on Monday night, Chicago will be looking really good. Nobody paying attention to the NFL hadn't seen how dominant Simmons is, but it was still impressive to see how quickly he fit in and made plays.

Chicago gets another close-up in prime time this week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night. Surprisingly, the Buccaneers are far better analytically than their 3-5 record would suggest. They're fifth in DVOA , eight spots ahead of the Bears, and eight in net EPA (expected points added) per play. The Bears are strong in net EPA, coming in third.

The Buccaneers will be completely overshadowed in this game. The Bears will be the focus on Sunday night as they've emerged as one of the NFL's most dangerous teams. That's a reason they're a healthy 6.5-point favorite. That's a lot of points, and the Buccaneers might be secretly pretty good. That's why Buccaneers +6.5 is the pick. And if the Bears blow out Tampa Bay in a big prime-time window, they'll take over as the talk of the NFL, if they're not already.

Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 9 of the NFL season:

The Bengals and Falcons go to Madrid, Spain, for this one. The Falcons are nearly impossible to figure out. They followed up a win over the undefeated 49ers by losing to a Buccaneers team that didn't complete a pass. That sums up Atlanta's season. We should trust Joe Burrow, who is on a heater, though there are more questions about Cincinnati's defense after it gave up 36 points to the Titans at home last week.

Maybe Joe Milton III gives Philadelphia a boost and the Eagles get their first win since Week 2. But since Jalen Hurts went on IR, the Eagles have lost all three games by double digits. It's not a good team in any way, and Milton is far from a sure thing. The Giants are off a bye and should be feeling good coming into this one.

The Broncos are the better team. A few things work against them in this spot: It's an early start on the East Coast, and the Panthers have three days rest advantage. The Broncos are also coming off an emotional win over the Chiefs and there could be a letdown. Denver has been much better at home this season. Carolina has faded after a good start but this is a decent opportunity for a win.

Give Miami credit for playing hard. Maybe at some point that effort starts to fade, but the last time they truly got blown out was Week 2. They lost by 14 points to the Chiefs, but Kansas City led by only seven points with three minutes left. It's possible the Lions score enough to cover, but remember that they're usually a different team outdoors.

Kansas City will enjoy the breather after facing the Seattle and Denver defenses on the road the past two weeks. This seems like the type of game in which the Chiefs could take out their frustrations on an opponent that does have some talent but has won only once since Week 1.

The Browns are likely going with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback because Deshaun Watson was put in concussion protocol. It's not like Watson was playing so well he's irreplaceable, but Sanders has thrown only three passes all season. The Saints are well rested coming off a bye. The Saints are not a great team this season, but this might be a spot for them to get right.

Is it time to trust the Rams? They have covered two games in a row without a sweat. Those wins came against mediocre (Raiders) or bad (Chargers) teams, but they did handle business. And the Commanders are mediocre at best and maybe just bad. Let's see if the Rams are truly back.

It is incredibly hard to trust the Cowboys, especially as a road favorite. But what we saw from the Colts last week in a 42-7 loss was troubling. There was no fight left in that team, which has lost key players to trades and knows its season is done. This could be a bad mistake, trusting a defense that can't stop anyone to cover almost a touchdown on the road. Taking the Colts at this point is even harder.

It's a lot for Houston to be favored by this much on the road, however, home-field advantage has been mostly eliminated this NFL season and the Chargers have no home-field advantage — even if that was still a thing. Houston is coming off a bye and still has hopes to revive its season. The Texans still have a 34.4% chance to make the playoffs according to DVOA. The Chargers are 0.0% on that list. They'll cover a spread at some point but it's hard to anticipate when it happens.

The Raiders have four losses, and they came against four of the better teams in the NFL: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills and Rams. The bad news is this week they get the Super Bowl favorites. The 49ers should be getting many players back after their bye. But the Raiders can move the ball and they're getting a lot of points.

With all the quarterback chaos this week, we get two teams that had a different quarterback in Week 8. Brissett was benched and traded, and Gardner Minshew II takes over. Sam Darnold has a quad injury and he'll be out, with Drew Lock taking over. Lock is a reasonable replacement, and Minshew isn't facing the Cowboys defense this week.

The Patriots have a lot of injuries and the Packers have a few days of extra rest. In a game that seems evenly matched, the small edges add up. Green Bay started the season very slow but has looked much better over the last four games, winning three and barely losing at Detroit. New England has also emerged after an early-season slump to win four of five. This is a really fun matchup, and even enough to feel OK taking the points.

This is an interesting game because the teams have opposite strengths. The Bills have a great offense and bad defense, and the Vikings have a bad offense and great defense. The Minnesota defense held the Bears to three points after all; Chicago has scored 30 points in every other Caleb Williams start. It will be a great test against Josh Allen, who is having another fantastic season. It's never enjoyable to be going against Allen, but getting 3.5 points with a defense this good seems right … as long as the offense does at least a little bit.

articles.title: Lions Players Honor Jack Campbell After Linebacker Was Hospitalized with Neck Injury
articles.summary: Members of the Detroit Lions wore Jack Campbell's No. 46 jersey as they arrived at Hard Rock Stadium for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body:
Members of the Detroit Lions wore Jack Campbell's No. 46 jersey as they arrived at Hard Rock Stadium for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.

Campbell remains hospitalized due to the neck injury he suffered in the team's 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings. The Lions officially placed him on injured reserve Saturday.

On Wednesday, the team released a statement from Campbell, who said he's "incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time."

"I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body," he said. "I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better."

Campbell's alma mater honored him Saturday. Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz said he set aside one of the game balls from the 24-10 win over Northwestern for the 2022 Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year.

Campbell, a first-round pick in the 2023 NFL draft, is in his fourth year with the Lions. An All-Pro and Pro Bowler a season ago, he signed an $81 million extension in May.

articles.title: Lions pay tribute to injured linebacker Jack Campbell a week after he was carted off field
articles.summary: Jack Campbell was stretchered off the field after a brutal tackle in Week 8.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions are letting linebacker Jack Campbell know he is in their thoughts. A week after Campbell was carted off the field and hospitalized, multiple members of the Lions showed up for Sunday's game wearing his jersey.

The team shared a few images prior to its Week 9 game against the Miami Dolphins.

Campbell was stretchered off the field after making a tackle during the team's Week 8 game against the Minnesota Vikings. It was clear immediately Campbell had sustained a significant injury on the play, as his arms went limp and he lay motionless on the field. Eventually, the entire Lions team came out and knelt around Campbell. Some members of the team were emotional. He was later ruled out with a neck injury.

The linebacker was taken to a local hospital and was said to be making positive progress early in the week. On Wednesday, he released a statement of his own, saying he had movement in his lower body and was "continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body."

Campbell, who is in his fourth year with the team, was off to a strong start after making the All-Pro team last season. Through seven games, he had 57 combined tackles prior to the injury.

It's unclear when Campbell will return to the team. While he's out, however, Campbell will remain on the minds of his teammates. The Lions made sure to send that message Sunday.

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase & Tee Higgins Shine, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Burrow, Bijan, Bengals-Falcons
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals' offensive firepower apparently travels well.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals' offensive firepower apparently travels well.

Cincinnati wasted no time setting the offensive tone during Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons at Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain, and took a 24-10 lead into halftime thanks in large part to Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

Burrow marched the Bengals on long touchdown drives in each of their first three possessions and a field goal on their fourth, capping the first one with a 47-yard strike to Chase, finishing the second one with his own rushing touchdown on a sneak play and then finding Higgins for a four-yard score on the third one.

While Higgins worked underneath routes on most of his early involvement, the Falcons secondary looked lost trying to prevent Chase from finding space downfield.

The star receiver eclipsed the century mark in yardage well before halftime as he blew by press coverage, came down with contested catches, made an incredible reception along the sidelines and put on an absolute show.

Offense has never been the issue in Cincinnati, though.

Defense has been at times, and it was Sunday as well when the Falcons scored the game's first touchdown when Michael Penix Jr. found Charlie Woerner for a score after star running back Bijan Robinson did much of the heavy lifting yardage wise.

Robinson also got involved in the aerial attack, although the Bengals defense improved in the second quarter after giving up 10 points in the first.

Even a mediocre defense should be enough for the Bengals to remain on the short list of Super Bowl contenders given all the offensive firepower they bring to the table, and that was on full display throughout the first half of Sunday's contest.

articles.title: New Odell Beckham Jr. Rumors on Vikings Contract and Roster Status Ahead of MNF vs. Bills
articles.summary: After spending the past month on the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad, veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. could finally get his chance to see some game action.
articles.body:
After spending the past month on the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad, veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. could finally get his chance to see some game action.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reported that the Vikings are signing Beckham to the 53-man roster ahead of their matchup against the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football .

The Vikings have an opening on offense after veteran wideout Jauan Jennings was ruled out for Monday night's game after suffering a strained calf in practice this week. His injury came after star quarterback Kyler Murray was sidelined with a hamstring injury, thrusting veteran backup Carson Wentz into the starting role against the Bills.

Beckham started the 2026 season with the New York Giants, but he didn't record a single catch in any of the three games he played before he was released in late September. He signed with Minnesota's practice squad a week after his departure from New York.

ESPN's Kevin Seifert reported on Saturday that Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said the team is "working through whether [Beckham] will be active Monday night." The Bills rank 24th in the NFL with 352.1 yards allowed per game, so Wentz would benefit from having an extra weapon against a subpar defense.

Minnesota is coming off its first loss of the season last week against the Detroit Lions, and Murray's absence will certainly make things more difficult against Buffalo. If Beckham gets his chance on the main roster, he will certainly be motivated to prove that he deserves to stay.

articles.title: What MSU football coach Pat Fitzgerald said about win over Michigan
articles.summary: Everything Pat Fitzgerald said about his team's upset win over Michigan
articles.body:
While it may have been said a little flippantly, there was some truth in Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham's comments earlier this week that the Michigan vs. Michigan State football game on Saturday was MSU's 'Super Bowl' . The Spartans had failed to win a Big Ten game this season, and a win over their rivals on the road would drastically change the vibes around the program. And that's exactly what Pat Fitzgerald and his Spartans did on Saturday, knocking off the Wolverines in the Big House 15 to 6 to earn their first conference win of the Pat Fitzgerald era.

After the game, a fired-up Pat Fitzgerald spoke to the media, and you can see his comments below:

Opening statement (0:47): "The credit goes to the man in the arena, and that's our players.… They're the definition of one of our values, which is respond."

To Spartan fans (1:51): "To the Spartan Dawgs, to all of our former players, and to the Spartan Nation, this one's for you."

On what outsiders think (2:35): "I'd love to tell you I really give a [expletive] what other people think, to be honest with you. I don't know if you heard, I got fired a couple years ago. And so that's where that [expletive] went out the window." The transcript drops the word here, so check the audio.

On the rebuild (3:01): "We're trying to build something here on bedrock, and we have not gotten the wins, and I understand that, and I own that. But … the pedal is down, and it's not going to stop."

For the seniors (3:25): "They had not been successful in this game, and how important this game was for those guys and to get Paul Bunyan back in East Lansing is for them."

On the 17-play, 10:41 drive (4:27): "Yeah, that was cool, wasn't it?"

Perspective (13:31): "I know we're not going to Indianapolis, and I know we're not competing for a Big Ten championship. Today was a state championship, and we went 1-0, and that's all that mattered today."

On November (10:30): "They forget what you did in September and October, and they remember what you did in November. And this is a great first step."

On kicking field goals instead of going for it (17:15): "Scared money don't make money.… I told you guys I will be aggressive but not reckless.… I thought we had the upper hand defensively."

On the handshake line and sideline behavior (18:29): "I did see when I looked over to the left that some guys didn't do that. So that'll be addressed.… One of the best compliments I've ever gotten was by the chain crew tonight. They said this is the best sideline they've ever had in a rivalry game."

articles.title: NFL rumors: Commanders not totally out of Brandon Aiyuk business as 49ers status hangs in air
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline is already living up to expectations. There have already been some massive trades ahead of the deadline, including a blockbuster...
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is already living up to expectations. There have already been some massive trades ahead of the deadline, including a blockbuster deal involving Jeffery Simmons . Could one of the league's most controversial veteran players finally be on the move after more than a year of off-the-field drama?

NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport shared intel from around the league ahead of the trade deadline. They explained that the Commanders are still not completely out of Brandon Aiyuk .

"The Commanders haven't completely abandoned the idea of adding wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, who was rumored during the summer to end up in Washington, according to sources," Schefter and Rapoport wrote on Sunday. "Before an Aiyuk deal could happen — if it were to happen — the organization would have to have discussions with multiple people. It's not a no, but it's also not a yes just yet."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Aiyuk has not suited up in the NFL since the 2024 season. He suffered a serious knee injury and missed multiple team meetings. As a result, the 49ers voided roughly $27 million of guarantees on Aiyuk's contract. Understandably, the relationship between both sides is now quite contentious.

Aiyuk is attempting to get reinstated to play in the NFL this season. But some experts like ESPN's Jeremy Fowler are skeptical that Aiyuk will be reinstated anytime soon.

"Aiyuk wants to get reinstated to play in the NFL. His prospects in the short term are not promising, assuming he becomes a free agent eventually," Fowler said.

As for the Commanders, they are 2-4-1 and still technically alive in the NFC East. Wide receiver is still a position of need, especially with Terry McLaurin on injured reserve . Aiyuk could be the solution Washington is looking for, so long as he is locked in on reviving his NFL career.

It will be interesting to see what happens next in the Aiyuk saga.

The NFL trade deadline is 4 p.m. ET on November 10th. Any potential Aiyuk move must come before that deadline.

articles.title: NFL trade rumors tracker: Live updates on news for Jonathan Taylor, Derrick Henry and more before 2026 deadline
articles.summary: The Sporting News is tracking live updates on the latest NFL trade rumors ahead of the 2026 deadline.
articles.body:
NFL trade season started early, as Jeffery Simmons, Marvin Harrison Jr., Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner all found themselves on the move well in advance of the Nov. 10 deadline.

As the final buzzer approaches, though, contenders are looking to best position themselves to make a run.

The top name on the market might be Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, who told the team he doesn't want to be traded but might not have much of a choice as Indianapolis' season spirals. Other teams, including the Cowboys and Eagles , have interesting decisions to make on their path forward as they weigh whether to trade stars.

The Sporting News is tracking live updates on the latest NFL trade rumors ahead of the 2026 deadline. Follow along below with the news.

NFL trades completed before 2026 deadline

Nov. 4 : The Arizona Cardinals traded QB Jacoby Brissett and a fifth-round pick to the Baltimore Ravens for a fourth-round pick and a seventh-round pick.

Oct. 29 : The Tennessee Titans traded DT Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chicago Bears for two first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-round pick.

Oct. 27 : The Indianapolis Colts traded DT DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers for a fourth-round pick.

Oct. 27 : The Indianapolis Colts traded OG Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks for third- and fifth-round picks.

Oct. 11 : The Arizona Cardinals traded WR Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans for second- and sixth-round picks.

Oct. 7 : The Philadelphia Eagles traded OG Cam Jurgens and a seventh-round pick to the Baltimore Ravens for a 2028 second-round pick and 2027 fifth-round pick.

Sept. 30 : The Pittsburgh Steelers traded CB Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys for a 2028 second-round pick and 2027 sixth-round pick.

Sept. 28 : The Minnesota Vikings traded QB J.J. McCarthy to the New York Giants for a 2027 fifth-round pick.

Latest NFL trade rumors before 2026 deadline

Nov. 8 — Josina Anderson reports that the Giants have "cooled" on Jonathan Taylor talks due to the Colts' high asking price. There are still a few days until the trade deadline, but for now, it appears New York will look elsewhere.

Nov. 8 — Although they are the last team without a win this season, the Chargers don't appear interested in trading players like Khalil Mack, Ladd McConkey, or, especially, Justin Herbert. Adam Schefter reports Los Angeles doesn't like the optics of giving up on the year.

Nov. 8 — According to Adam Schefter, Baltimore is turning down trade requests for the veteran running back despite the team's recent losing streak.

Nov. 7 — While the Colts have received calls about Daniel Jones, Tom Pelissero reports that so far, Indianapolis has "told interested teams they aren't trading him."

Broncos consider making audacious move for Cardinals star Trey McBride

Nov. 7 — ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Denver checked in on McBride, a Fort Morgan, Colorado native who starred at Colorado State. The Cardinals summarily declined the proposal, proclaiming they had no interest in letting their star man go.

Multiple teams have inquired about Daniel Jones' availability, per report

Nov. 7 — Jones is the latest in a string of Colts players to garner trade deadline interest, with NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reporting that Indianapolis had received multiple calls regarding its QB's availability.

Derrick Henry could be on the move after Ravens' blowout loss

Nov. 6 —Henry, who is a free agent after the season, was frustrated by Baltimore's fourth straight loss on Thursday night in the Ravens' last game before the trade deadline. With Baltimore facing most of the season without Lamar Jackson, the team could decide to get draft capital back for Henry instead of keeping him for the remainder of the season.

Conflicting reports over Giants' willingness to play ball with Colts for Jonathan Taylor

Nov. 5 — Taylor remains the name on the lips of decision-makers ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, with SNY's Connor Hughes reporting that sources not connected to the Giants are unsure of whether New York will attempt to make a move for the Colts standout. Some believe head coach John Harbaugh wants to move aggressively to land the former Offensive Player of the Year winner. Others believe Indianapolis' asking price will prove too cost-prohibitive for the Giants — or any other side — to seek out his services.

Colts to wait until after Week 9 before exploring trades for Jonathan Taylor, others

Nov. 5 — The Colts have been monitoring interest in a series of players, headlined by Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs. However, according to insider Jordan Schultz , Indianapolis doesn't plan on making a move until after its Week 9 game vs. the Cowboys. It appears that if teams want to strike a deal with the Colts, they'll have to work quickly on Monday and Tuesday.

Ravens acquiring Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals

Nov. 4 — The Ravens are finalizing a deal to acquire QB Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports , though it won't be completed in time for Brissett to join the team before Thursday's game. Compensation has not yet been reported.

Colts' asking price for Taylor remains high

Nov. 4 — The Colts are still asking for a first-round pick for Jonathan Taylor and maintaining that they don't have to trade him, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports , while suitors believe a second-round pick plus another asset should be enough.

Nov. 4 — ESPN's Dan Graziano reports teams were watching the Jets last weekend, wondering whether another loss might open the door for players such as Will McDonald IV to become available. With Braelon Allen's breakout in Breece Hall's absence, Hall could be another trade candidate.

Nov. 3 — Cardinals pass-rusher Josh Sweat is open to the possibility of being traded, according to Jordan Schultz . Sweat, whose name surfaced in rumors leading up to the season, had 12 sacks in 2025 but has seen his production dip this year.

Teams intrigued by George Pickens' situation

Nov. 2 — People around the NFL are wondering whether the Cowboys might make George Pickens available, Jordan Schultz reports . While there is no firm indication Dallas is looking to trade Pickens or anyone, the team's lack of success and Pickens' expiring contract could put a deal on the table.

Nov. 1 — Jordan Schultz reports the Broncos, Vikings, Packers, Bengals and Giants are among teams who have reached out to the Colts about Jonathan Taylor. Schultz believes a trade is "more likely than not" despite Indianapolis' asking price being too high for most teams at the moment.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. signs with NFL contender in Week 9
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr. is back on an NFL team's active roster after securing another opportunity to continue his career.
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr. has secured another opportunity to continue his NFL career after returning to the league earlier this season. The veteran wide receiver is now set for a bigger role with a team that has ambitions of making a deep postseason run.

Beckham previously joined the Minnesota Vikings after a brief stint with the New York Giants. His latest move gives him a chance to become a more permanent part of Minnesota's offense.

Vikings promote Odell Beckham Jr. to 53-man roster

The Vikings are signing Beckham to their 53-man roster (h/t Tom Pelissero of The Ringer).

The 34-year-old receiver initially joined Minnesota's practice squad in October. He now has a place on the active roster as the Vikings prepare for their Week 9 matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

Beckham played a limited role during his three-game return to New York, recording no catches on just one target before the Giants released him.

Minnesota offered him another opportunity, partly because of his previous relationship with head coach Kevin O'Connell. The two worked together with the Los Angeles Rams during their Super Bowl-winning 2021 campaign.

Beckham gets another chance to revive his NFL career

Beckham's move to the active roster gives him a clearer path to contributing to the Vikings' offense. His experience could prove useful as Minnesota looks to maintain its position among the NFC's contenders.

The receiver has previously played for the Giants, Cleveland Browns, Rams, Baltimore Ravens and Miami Dolphins. His most successful stretch came in New York, where he quickly established himself as one of the league's most recognizable receivers.

However, injuries and inconsistent production have affected the later stages of his career.

His promotion to the 53-man roster gives him another opportunity to prove he still has something to offer at the highest level.
